The content spans carry the family's declared normalisation (client.template normalize: [strip]): fit strips the spans before measuring and the wire ships them stripped - the paper's query.strip()/doc.strip() - the reference's spans agree byte for byte on every under-cap row, and the template file carries no jinja trim filter. The research's strip asymmetry (report section 6 row 1) closes as declared policy here, one rule for the family. Known served-vs-reference differences, all inherited from the paper's own paths and recorded in the research report section 6/7: (1) the reference truncates only the whole rendered prompt at 8192 from the right (declared known_deviations: anchor_drop_over_cap), the served path cuts the content spans and keeps the assistant header; (2) the settle rule (above) settles a query over its 4096-token share served-side while the in-process reference keeps it whole - the r-zerank1 research measured 904 prompt tokens lost at a 5000-token query under the former engine-side constant; over-share queries are declared divergence rows - an over-share query in an UNDER-budget pair is an under-cap row and gates red by design (the reference never ports the client's settle rule), so the wave's pairs files keep queries well within the share and drop any row stage 1 goes red on; (3) the score-head matmul runs in fp32 on the engine (head_dtype default for pooling) and bf16 in the reference - expected well inside the probability gates; --hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "model"}' is the closer-to-reference option if the gate ever fails. The paper's last prompt token is the newline after the assistant header (dropping it flips the render: the research lane's mutation M1); the template file ends with the header inside every branch. Budget: max_tokens 8192 is the paper's MAX_SEQ_LENGTH, counted as the engine sees the whole prompt (frame + query + document; the frame's fixed overhead measures 13 tokens on this tokenizer, add_special_tokens adds none - both measured); query_max_tokens 4096 is the query's settled share (the settle rule above).
